topic: Data centers and the PJM capacity auction behind rising power bills

sources.title: DOE Releases New Report Evaluating Increase in Electricity Demand from Data Centers (LBNL 2024 report)
Projected data center growth spurs PJM capacity prices by factor of 10
sources.cites: PJM auction results; Monitoring Analytics (PJM's independent market monitor); D.C. Office of the People's Counsel

sources.title: PJM Auction Procures 134,479 MW of Generation Resources (17 Dec 2025)
Data center power demands again drive record power auction prices (17 Dec 2025)
Are AI Datacenters Increasing Electric Bills for American Households?

claims.text: Data centers used about 4.4% of US electricity in 2023 and are expected to use about 6.7-12% by 2028 (LBNL report for DOE).
claims.quote: data centers consumed about 4.4% of total U.S. electricity in 2023 and are expected to consume approximately 6.7 to 12% of total U.S. electricity by 2028
claims.label: LBNL estimate

claims.text: PJM serves more than 67 million people across 13 states and the District of Columbia.
claims.quote: to meet projected electricity needs for more than 67 million people across 13 states and the District of Columbia; which spans all or parts of 13 mid-Atlantic and Midwestern states, plus the District of Columbia

claims.text: PJM's capacity market is a forward auction that pays for enough power plant capacity to meet forecast peak demand.
claims.quote: The capacity market is a forward auction that seeks to ensure there is enough power plant capacity on the system to meet projected load; available to serve forecasted peak electricity demand, plus a reserve margin

claims.text: PJM capacity prices (rest of RTO): $28.92/MW-day for 2024/25, $269.92 for 2025/26, $329.17 for 2026/27, $333.44 (the cap) for 2027/28.
claims.quote: RTO prices were down from $34.13/MW-day to $28.92/MW-day; 2025/2026 delivery year (June 1, 2025-May 31, 2026): $269.92/MW-day in most zones; 2026/2027 delivery year (June 1, 2026-May 31, 2027): $329.17/MW-day in all zones; The price came in at the FERC-approved cap, $333.44/MW-day (UCAP) for the entire PJM footprint; again set an all-time record high clearing price of $333 per megawatt-day

claims.text: Without the cap, PJM's simulation says the 2027/28 price would have cleared at $529.80/MW-day.
claims.quote: For the 2027/2028 simulated BRA, all prices cleared at $529.80 except the DOM LDA which cleared at $542

claims.text: Forecast PJM demand rose sharply with data centers: IEEFA ties it to the AI boom between the Dec 2022 and Jul 2024 auctions; for 2027/28 nearly 5,100 of 5,250 MW of forecast growth is data centers.
claims.quote: Between December 2022 and July 2024, the artificial intelligence (AI) bubble took off driving a dramatic increase in forecasted energy consumption in PJM; Nearly 5,100 MW of that increase is attributable to data center demand

claims.text: PJM's independent market monitor (Monitoring Analytics) estimated data centers caused 63% of the 2025/26 price increase: $9.3 billion recovered from customers.
claims.quote: estimated that data centers were responsible for 63% of the increase in prices in the 2025/2026 auction, which translates to $9.3 billion in costs that will be recovered from customers across PJM in higher electric rates
claims.label: market monitor's estimate

claims.text: Pepco residential customers in D.C. saw bills rise an average $21/month from June 2025; the D.C. consumer counsel estimates about half ($10) is from capacity prices.
claims.quote: Pepco residential customers saw their bills go up by an average of $21/month starting in June 2025; estimates that $10/month, or about half of this increase, is due to the spike in capacity market prices
claims.label: consumer counsel's estimate

claims.text: SemiAnalysis argues the bill rise is mostly due to market design rather than AI itself; Texas, with similar data-center growth and no capacity auction, saw futures move only a few percent.
claims.quote: In short, empirically the fault is government policy, not AI; Yet power futures in Texas have moved only a few percent in the past year
claims.label: one analysis
claims.note: Context for the risk note; not used in the script.

myths.myth: Data centers raise your bill by using your electricity.
myths.truth: The main channel in PJM is the capacity auction: forecast data-center demand raised the price every customer pays for standby power plants.
